prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S815: The Slot Coordinator shall own slot allocation reference data, including Calculated Takeoff Time tolerances and Slot Compliance State definitions.
S816: The Airport Duty Manager shall own airport capacity declarations, including Airport Capacity Plan records and Airport Acceptance Rate values.
S817: The Tower Supervisor shall own tower sequence status data maintained for the Tower Sequence Manager.
S818: The Ramp Control Lead shall own ramp movement status data maintained for the Ramp Movement Board.
S819: The Meteorology Briefing Officer shall own operational weather classification inputs accepted by the Weather Ingest Gateway.
S820: The Airline Operations Coordinator shall be accountable for airline-supplied schedule intent, readiness status, and Target Off Block Time updates submitted through approved interfaces.
S821: Each owned data element shall have a defined business meaning, allowed value range, update authority, retention class, and escalation contact.
S822: Freshness indicators shall be displayed on the Common Situation Display wherever stale data could affect sequencing, metering, regulation, or resource allocation decisions.
S823: The freshness indicator shall include the time of last accepted update, the maximum permitted age, and a visual state that distinguishes current, aging, stale, and unavailable data.
S824: The Time Synchronization Service shall provide the common time basis used for freshness calculations across the Regional Flow Platform.
S825: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, and Departure Metering Service shall reject data that lacks a trusted timestamp.
S826: Validation rules shall include schema checks, mandatory field checks, code set checks, temporal sequence checks, and operational plausibility checks.
S827: The Flight Data Exchange shall validate Flight Intent Message content before the data is made available for operational use.
S828: The Surface Surveillance Adapter shall apply position quality checks and shall mark uncertain observations before they are used by surface decision functions.
S829: The Airline Interface Adapter shall apply carrier-specific format checks while preserving the common operational meaning required by the Regional Flow Platform.
S830: The Handling Resource Planner shall validate resource quantities, task timing, and allocation identifiers against active operational reference data.
S831: The Business Rules Registry shall hold the current validation thresholds, allowable reason codes, and exception rules approved for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, and Contingency Fallback State.
S832: When a discrepancy is detected, the affected component shall mark the data as disputed and shall preserve the prior accepted value until an authorized correction is available.
S833: The Data Governance Steward shall coordinate discrepancy resolution with the responsible operational owner and shall record the disposition in the Audit Event Ledger.
S834: Urgent discrepancies that could change a metering, arrival regulation, or slot allocation decision shall be raised through the Alert Distribution Hub and reviewed in the Digital Briefing Room.
S835: The System Support Engineer shall investigate technical causes of missing, delayed, duplicated, or transformed records and shall provide evidence needed for stewardship decisions.
S836: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall retain data quality measures, including validation failure rates, freshness breaches, manual corrections, and recurring ownership conflicts.
S837: Stewardship reviews shall use those measures to update training, adjust validation rules, and improve the reliability of information used in operational decision making.
S838: Performance measurement for the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System shall convert operational events into repeatable indicators that can be reviewed after each operating day.
S839: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall calculate delay absorption as the portion of expected airborne or terminal-area delay that is converted into controlled ground delay before departure.
S840: Delay absorption shall be measured by comparing the unconstrained demand predicted by the Demand Prediction Service with the regulated demand produced by the Slot Allocation Engine and the realized movement times captured through the Flight Data Exchange.
S841: The principal delay absorption indicator shall report minutes absorbed at origin, minutes remaining in the arrival stream, and minutes transferred to surface queues within the region.
S842: The Regional Flow Manager shall use this indicator to verify that a Ground Delay Program reduced airborne holding without creating excessive departure congestion at constrained airports.
S843: Queue length performance shall be measured for runway departure queues, arrival metering queues, apron movement queues, and regulation waiting lists.
S844: The Tower Sequence Manager shall provide runway sequence counts, while the Ramp Movement Board shall provide surface queue counts based on movement status and surveillance confirmation.
S845: The North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, and West Apron Sensor shall support independent checks of queue length where surveillance coverage is available.
S846: Queue metrics shall include maximum queue length, average queue length, time above threshold, and recovery time after a constraint is lifted.
S847: Slot adherence shall be measured as the difference between actual movement times and the assigned Calculated Takeoff Time or Target Off Block Time.
S848: The Slot Coordinator shall review slot adherence by operator, airport, time band, and regulation identifier to detect recurring causes of noncompliance.
